Definition: from G4413 and G2515; a sitting first (in the front row), i.e. preeminence in council:--chief (highest, uppermost) seat.
BiblicalUsage: Protokathadria is the chief seat, the first place in the council or the synagogue. Jesus said the scribes and Pharisees love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the marketplaces, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the chief seat is the test of the heart: the Pharisees loved to be seen first, and Jesus loved to be last. I hold that the seat I want tells me who I serve, because the one who wants the first seat is serving himself.
